scores.name: Coverage
scores.rationale: All five business rules (partial refund cap, 14-day routing without interchange penalty, fraud screening for high-risk accounts, settled-dispute denial, immutable audit logging with idempotency keys) are covered across functional, negative, boundary, validation, and data categories with sensible proportions (29 cases). Boundary coverage includes day 14 vs day 15 and the 1.5% ratio exactly-at-threshold, and rule-interaction/edge scenarios (high-risk + settled dispute in TC-027, idempotency race in TC-028, true log-immutability in TC-026, a measurable interchange-fee field in TC-029) are all present. Missing: a cumulative multi-refund over-limit scenario and a just-above-threshold chargeback ratio case.

scores.name: Completeness
scores.rationale: Every case has concrete preconditions, ordered steps, and a specific, verifiable expected result, including the previously-hard-to-verify audit-log immutability (TC-026 attempts an actual modify/delete) and interchange-fee exemption (TC-029 checks a named field equal to 0). A few expected results still rely on generic phrasing ('an error indicating...') rather than a concrete status/error code, slightly reducing verifiability, though this is largely unavoidable given the source requirement supplies no response formats.

scores.name: Traceability
scores.rationale: Every case carries requirement_reference REQ-089 and no orphan cases exist, but traceability is only at the whole-requirement level; there is no per-rule tag (e.g. BR-1..BR-5) linking each case to the specific bullet it exercises, making it harder to audit that every individual business rule has proportionate, explicit case coverage.

scores.name: Correctness
scores.rationale: Expected results align with the literal wording of the requirement's rules, and the suite is transparent about assumptions (14-day inclusivity, 1.5% exclusivity, denial precedence, an invented 'interchange_fee' field, idempotency conflict handling), with those assumptions now exercised concretely (TC-026 through TC-029). However, the quality_report rates acceptance_criteria as 'bad' with no defined API responses, error codes, or field names, so several expected results (the interchange_fee field name, fraud-screening-vs-dispute precedence, replay-vs-conflict idempotency semantics) are necessarily invented rather than derived from the requirement, capping how 'correct' they can be judged.

scores.name: Uniqueness
scores.rationale: Cases are genuinely distinct scenarios rather than reworded duplicates; even similar-looking pairs (e.g. TC-012/TC-013 day 14 vs day 15, TC-009/TC-024 same-params replay vs different-params conflict, TC-004/TC-027 fraud screening alone vs combined with settled dispute) test materially different conditions and outcomes.

overall.verdict: A thorough, well-documented suite given a poorly specified requirement; add per-rule traceability tags and a cumulative over-limit refund case, and request concrete error/status codes to raise correctness further.

gaps.detail: No case verifies that a refund request is rejected when it would push the cumulative refunded amount over the original transaction total across multiple sequential partial refunds (only a single-request overage is tested in TC-008); this is a realistic variant of the partial-refund cap rule that is not exercised.

TC-014 tests a chargeback ratio of exactly 1.5% (fraud screening not triggered) but no case tests a ratio just above the threshold (e.g. 1.51%) to confirm fraud screening is triggered on the other side of the boundary, leaving the '> 1.5%' boundary only half-verified.

Test cases reference only the overall requirement (REQ-089) and not the specific business rule bullet each one targets, so it is not possible to programmatically verify that each of the five bullets has proportionate, auditable coverage without manually reading every case.

recommendations.detail: Add a test case where a transaction of 200.00 has already been partially refunded to 190.00, and a further refund request for 20.00 is submitted; expect rejection because the cumulative refunded amount (210.00) would exceed the original transaction total, verifying the partial-refund cap is enforced across multiple sequential requests, not just a single oversized request.

Add a boundary test case for a merchant account with a chargeback ratio of exactly 1.51% (just above the 1.5% threshold), expecting the automated fraud screening step to be invoked, to complement the existing at-threshold case that confirms screening is skipped at exactly 1.5%.

Add a 'rule_id' or similar field to every test case mapping it to the specific business rule bullet it exercises (e.g. BR-1 partial refund cap, BR-2 14-day routing/interchange exemption, BR-3 fraud screening, BR-4 settled-dispute denial, BR-5 audit logging/idempotency), so per-rule coverage can be verified directly instead of relying only on the blanket REQ-089 reference.

Where expected results currently use generic language such as 'an error indicating...' (e.g. TC-007, TC-008, TC-011, TC-017 through TC-020), replace with a concrete, consistently-applied status/error code convention (e.g. HTTP 409 for settled-dispute denial, HTTP 422 for amount validation errors) so expected results are precisely verifiable rather than assumed at test-execution time.
